{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14年}} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Sōja shrines}}{{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]]
