{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine Ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14th year }} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Shinto-stub}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Maebashi]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] }} [[sn:Sōja Shrine (Maebashi)]] [[sn:ōja Shrine (Maebashi)]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Pages without valid translation templates or en interwikis]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Sōja Shrine (Maebashi)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:Pages without valid translation templates or en interwikis or ja interwikis]] [[ja:総社神社 (前橋市)]]

{{神社 |名称 = 總社神社 |画像 = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px]]
境内 |所在地 = [[群馬県]][[前橋市]][[元総社町]]1丁目31番地45 |位置 = {{Coord|36|23|16.80|N|139|2|16.30|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=総社神社}} |祭神 = [[イワツツノオ|磐筒男命]]

[[スサノオ|須佐之男命]] |神体 = [[上野国神名帳]] |社格 = [[上野国]][[総社]]
旧[[県社]] |創建 = （伝）第10代[[崇神天皇]]年間 |本殿 = 三間社[[流造]] |別名 = 上野国総社神社 |札所等 = |例祭 = [[3月15日]] |神事 = 射儀式（[[1月6日]]）
御筒粥置炭式 （[[1月15日]]） |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Gunma|lat_deg=36|lat_min=23|lat_sec=16.80|lon_deg=139|lon_min=2|lon_sec=16.30|label=総社神社|position=top|width=200|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|36|23|16.8|N|139|2|16.3|E}}}} }} [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) torii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|鳥居]] '''総社神社'''（そうじゃじんじゃ）は、[[群馬県]][[前橋市]][[元総社町]]にある[[神社]]。[[上野国]][[総社]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]。 正式名称は「'''總社神社'''」群馬県神社庁サイトより。。国名を冠し「'''上野国総社神社'''（上野総社神社）」とも称する。 == 概要 == [[古代]]の[[国司]]の任務に神拝・朔幣というものが存在した。すなわち、神拝とは新任の国司が国内の主要な神社に参拝し[[奉幣]]を行うものであり、朔幣とは毎月朔日に国内の主要な神社に奉幣を行うものである{{Sfn|群馬県史編さん委員会|1993|pp=798-801}}。平安時代中期から後期にかけて、国司は[[国衙]]の近くに[[総社]]を興し、ここに幣帛を奉るようになった。[[上野国]]における総社が当社である。 国司が奉幣を行う神社を記載した公簿が[[国内神名帳]]であり、当社では明治時代まで『[[上野国神名帳]]』を[[神体]]として祀っていた{{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1971|p=644}}。同帳は群馬県指定重要文化財に指定されている。そのほか境内では、本殿が群馬県指定重要文化財に指定されている。 == 祭神 == '''主祭神''' * [[イワツツノオ|磐筒男命]] （いわつつのおのみこと） * 磐筒女命 （いわつつのめのみこと） * [[ウカノミタマ|宇迦之御魂命]] （うかのみたまのみこと） * [[経津主神|経津主命]] （ふつぬしのみこと） * [[スサノオ|須佐之男命]] （すさのおのみこと） '''相殿神''' : 『上野国神名帳』総社本に記される「鎮守十社」。 * 正一位 抜鉾大明神 - [[一之宮貫前神社]] * 正一位 赤城大明神 - [[赤城神社]] * 正一位 伊香保大明神 - [[伊香保神社]] * 正一位 岩根大明神 - 甲波宿禰神社 * 正一位 若伊香保大明神 - [[若伊香保神社]] * 正一位 榛名大明神 - [[榛名神社]] * 正一位 小祝大明神 - [[小祝神社]] * 従一位 火雷大明神 - [[火雷神社 (玉村町)|火雷神社]] * 従一位 倭文大明神 - [[倭文神社 (伊勢崎市)|倭文神社]] * 従一位 浅間大明神 - 浅間神社 '''配祀神''' * 上野国549社 {{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1984|pp=631-647}} == 歴史 == [[File:Miyanabe-jinja.JPG|thumb|200px|right|宮鍋神社（{{Coord|36|23|25.02|N|139|02|08.73|E|region:JP-10_type:landmark|name=宮鍋神社（旧社地伝承地）}}）
（国府伝承地・総社旧地伝承地）]] 社伝によると、[[崇神天皇]]皇子の[[豊城入彦命]]が軍神として[[経津主神|経津主命]]を祀ったことに始まるという{{Sfn|総社神社（平）|1987年}}{{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1984|pp=631-647}}。[[安閑天皇]]の時には上毛野小熊が社殿を改築して「蒼海明神」と称し、[[天平]]10年（[[738年]]）には上野国549社を合祀し「総社明神」と称したともいう{{Sfn|総社神社（平）|1987年}}{{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1984|pp=631-647}}。しかしながら、諸国の国府で国中の神々を合祀する風潮が生まれるのは[[律令制]]の衰退期であり、当社の成立年代はさらに下ると見られている{{Sfn|総社神社（平）|1987年}}。 当地に移る以前は、[[蒼海城]]内の宮ノ辺（宮鍋）の地にあったという{{Sfn|総社神社（平）|1987年}}{{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1984|pp=631-647}}。また、[[長享]]2年（[[1488年]]）に[[万里集九]]が当社を訪れて記述を残しているほか、[[永禄]]9年（[[1566年]]）に兵火で焼失、[[元亀]]年間（[[1570年]]-[[1573年]]）に現在地に再建されたという{{Sfn|総社神社（平）|1987年}}。[[弥勒菩薩]]を[[本地垂迹|本地仏]]として、[[天正]]14年（[[1586年]]）の紀年のある[[懸仏]]が所蔵されているが、[[普賢菩薩]]を刻んだ天正17年の銘のある懸仏も所蔵されている{{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1971|pp=772-780}}。 [[元和 (日本)|元和]]2年（[[1616年]]）[[総社藩|総社城]]主[[秋元泰朝]]により大修理をされたのが現在の総社神社本殿である{{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1984|pp=631-647}}。近世には朱印26石が与えられた{{Sfn|総社神社（平）|1987年}}。 [[明治]]に入り、[[近代社格制度]]では[[県社]]に列した。 == 境内 == [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) haiden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|拝殿（前橋市指定重要文化財）]] * 本殿 *: 間口三間・奥行二間の三間社[[流造]]。[[慶長]]年間の造営であるが桃山時代の様式を残し{{Sfn|尾崎|1974|pp=359-363}}、群馬県指定重要文化財に指定されている。 * 拝殿 *: [[天保]]14年（[[1843年]]）の再建で、前橋市指定重要文化財に指定されている。 File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) kaguraden.JPG|神楽殿 File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) sandou.JPG|参道 == 祭事 == * 正月元旦 （1月1日）祭事は[http://www.net-you.com/souja/shinji.html 年中行事と神事]（公式サイト）による。 * 射儀式 （1月6日） * 御筒粥置炭式 （1月15日） * [[追儺]]式 （2月節分） * 祈年祭 （2月20日） * 春季例祭 （3月15日） * [[大祓]]式 （6月30日） * 茅輪神事 （6月30日） * 秋期例祭 （10月9日） * [[七五三]] （10月-11月中頃） * 勤労感謝祭 （11月23日） * 御神迎式 （旧暦11月1日） * 大祓式 （12月31日） == 文化財 == === 群馬県指定文化財 === * 重要文化財 ** 本殿（建造物） - 昭和38年9月4日指定。 ** 総社神社[[懸仏]] 2面（工芸品） - 昭和49年12月23日指定。 ** [[雲版]] 1面（工芸品） - 昭和51年5月7日指定。 ** 総社本上野国神名帳 1巻（書跡） - 昭和49年12月23日指定。 === 前橋市指定文化財 === * 重要文化財 ** 拝殿 - 平成5年4月16日指定。 * 重要無形民俗文化財 ** 総社神社の筒粥置炭式 - 平成5年4月16日指定。 ** 総社神社[[神楽|太々神楽]] - 昭和48年9月24日指定。 * 天然記念物 ** 総社神社の社叢けやき 6本 - 平成9年4月21日指定。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[群馬県]][[前橋市]]元総社町1丁目31番地45 '''交通アクセス''' * 鉄道：[[東日本旅客鉄道|JR東日本]][[上越線]]・[[両毛線]] [[新前橋駅]] （徒歩約20分） * バス：[[群馬中央バス]]　[[前橋駅]]～[[立川町 (前橋市)|立川町]]通り～[[新前橋駅]]西口線　総社神社南バス停または明神前バス停下車すぐ == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 神社由緒書 * 現地説明板 * {{Cite book|和書 |title=上野国神名帳の研究 |date=1974-12-10 |year=1974 |publisher=尾崎先生著書刊行会 |author=尾崎喜左雄 |last=尾崎 |first=喜左雄 |author-link=尾崎喜左雄}} * {{Cite book|和書 |title=群馬県史 |date=1993-5-27 |year=1993 |publisher=群馬県 |editor=群馬県史編さん委員会 |volume=通史編2 原始古代2}} * {{Cite book|和書 |title=前橋市史 |date=1971-2-1 |year=1971 |publisher=前橋市 |editor=前橋市史編さん委員会 |volume=第一巻}} * {{Cite book|和書 |title=前橋市史 |date=1984-2-1 |year=1984 |publisher=前橋市 |editor=前橋市史編さん委員会 |volume=第五巻}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=明治神社誌料編纂所|author=|year=1912|chapter=總社神社|title=[[府県郷社明治神社誌料]]|publisher=明治神社誌料編纂所|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|明治神社誌料|1912年}}}} * [{{NDLDC|1088244/504}} 『明治神社誌料 府県郷社 上』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）504-505コマ参照。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1987|chapter=総社神社|title=日本歴史地名体系 10 群馬県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582490107|ref={{Harvid|総社神社（平）|1987年}}}} == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Souja-jinja (Maebashi)}} * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ 上野国総社神社]（公式サイト） * [https://www.city.maebashi.gunma.jp/soshiki/kyoiku/bunkazaihogo/gyomu/3/2/1/5117.html 元総社・東の文化財を訪ねて／前橋市] {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:そうしやしんしや}} [[Category:前橋市の歴史]] [[Category:前橋市の建築物]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:群馬県の旧県社]] [[Category:群馬県の神社]] [[Category:上野国|社0]] [[Category:群馬県指定重要文化財]] [[Category:群馬県内の市町村指定有形文化財]]

御筒粥置炭式 （[[1月15日]]） |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Gunma|lat_deg=36|lat_min=23|lat_sec=16.80|lon_deg=139|lon_min=2|lon_sec=16.30|label=総社神社|position=top|width=200|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|36|23|16.8|N|139|2|16.3|E}}}} }} [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) torii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|鳥居]] '''総社神社'''（そうじゃじんじゃ）は、[[群馬県]][[前橋市]][[元総社町]]にある[[神社]]。[[上野国]][[総社]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]。 正式名称は「'''總社神社'''」群馬県神社庁サイトより。。国名を冠し「'''上野国総社神社'''（上野総社神社）」とも称する。 == 概要 == [[古代]]の[[国司]]の任務に神拝・朔幣というものが存在した。すなわち、神拝とは新任の国司が国内の主要な神社に参拝し[[奉幣]]を行うものであり、朔幣とは毎月朔日に国内の主要な神社に奉幣を行うものである{{Sfn|群馬県史編さん委員会|1993|pp=798-801}}。平安時代中期から後期にかけて、国司は[[国衙]]の近くに[[総社]]を興し、ここに幣帛を奉るようになった。[[上野国]]における総社が当社である。 国司が奉幣を行う神社を記載した公簿が[[国内神名帳]]であり、当社では明治時代まで『[[上野国神名帳]]』を[[神体]]として祀っていた{{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1971|p=644}}。同帳は群馬県指定重要文化財に指定されている。そのほか境内では、本殿が群馬県指定重要文化財に指定されている。 == 祭神 == '''主祭神''' * [[イワツツノオ|磐筒男命]] （いわつつのおのみこと） * 磐筒女命 （いわつつのめのみこと） * [[ウカノミタマ|宇迦之御魂命]] （うかのみたまのみこと） * [[経津主神|経津主命]] （ふつぬしのみこと） * [[スサノオ|須佐之男命]] （すさのおのみこと） '''相殿神''' : 『上野国神名帳』総社本に記される「鎮守十社」。 * 正一位 抜鉾大明神 - [[一之宮貫前神社]] * 正一位 赤城大明神 - [[赤城神社]] * 正一位 伊香保大明神 - [[伊香保神社]] * 正一位 岩根大明神 - 甲波宿禰神社 * 正一位 若伊香保大明神 - [[若伊香保神社]] * 正一位 榛名大明神 - [[榛名神社]] * 正一位 小祝大明神 - [[小祝神社]] * 従一位 火雷大明神 - [[火雷神社 (玉村町)|火雷神社]] * 従一位 倭文大明神 - [[倭文神社 (伊勢崎市)|倭文神社]] * 従一位 浅間大明神 - 浅間神社 '''配祀神''' * 上野国549社 {{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1984|pp=631-647}} == 歴史 == [[File:Miyanabe-jinja.JPG|thumb|200px|right|宮鍋神社（{{Coord|36|23|25.02|N|139|02|08.73|E|region:JP-10_type:landmark|name=宮鍋神社（旧社地伝承地）}}）
（国府伝承地・総社旧地伝承地）]] 社伝によると、[[崇神天皇]]皇子の[[豊城入彦命]]が軍神として[[経津主神|経津主命]]を祀ったことに始まるという{{Sfn|総社神社（平）|1987年}}{{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1984|pp=631-647}}。[[安閑天皇]]の時には上毛野小熊が社殿を改築して「蒼海明神」と称し、[[天平]]10年（[[738年]]）には上野国549社を合祀し「総社明神」と称したともいう{{Sfn|総社神社（平）|1987年}}{{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1984|pp=631-647}}。しかしながら、諸国の国府で国中の神々を合祀する風潮が生まれるのは[[律令制]]の衰退期であり、当社の成立年代はさらに下ると見られている{{Sfn|総社神社（平）|1987年}}。 当地に移る以前は、[[蒼海城]]内の宮ノ辺（宮鍋）の地にあったという{{Sfn|総社神社（平）|1987年}}{{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1984|pp=631-647}}。また、[[長享]]2年（[[1488年]]）に[[万里集九]]が当社を訪れて記述を残しているほか、[[永禄]]9年（[[1566年]]）に兵火で焼失、[[元亀]]年間（[[1570年]]-[[1573年]]）に現在地に再建されたという{{Sfn|総社神社（平）|1987年}}。[[弥勒菩薩]]を[[本地垂迹|本地仏]]として、[[天正]]14年（[[1586年]]）の紀年のある[[懸仏]]が所蔵されているが、[[普賢菩薩]]を刻んだ天正17年の銘のある懸仏も所蔵されている{{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1971|pp=772-780}}。 [[元和 (日本)|元和]]2年（[[1616年]]）[[総社藩|総社城]]主[[秋元泰朝]]により大修理をされたのが現在の総社神社本殿である{{Sfn|前橋市史編さん委員会|1984|pp=631-647}}。近世には朱印26石が与えられた{{Sfn|総社神社（平）|1987年}}。 [[明治]]に入り、[[近代社格制度]]では[[県社]]に列した。 == 境内 == [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) haiden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|拝殿（前橋市指定重要文化財）]] * 本殿 *: 間口三間・奥行二間の三間社[[流造]]。[[慶長]]年間の造営であるが桃山時代の様式を残し{{Sfn|尾崎|1974|pp=359-363}}、群馬県指定重要文化財に指定されている。 * 拝殿 *: [[天保]]14年（[[1843年]]）の再建で、前橋市指定重要文化財に指定されている。 File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) kaguraden.JPG|神楽殿 File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) sandou.JPG|参道 == 祭事 == * 正月元旦 （1月1日）祭事は[http://www.net-you.com/souja/shinji.html 年中行事と神事]（公式サイト）による。 * 射儀式 （1月6日） * 御筒粥置炭式 （1月15日） * [[追儺]]式 （2月節分） * 祈年祭 （2月20日） * 春季例祭 （3月15日） * [[大祓]]式 （6月30日） * 茅輪神事 （6月30日） * 秋期例祭 （10月9日） * [[七五三]] （10月-11月中頃） * 勤労感謝祭 （11月23日） * 御神迎式 （旧暦11月1日） * 大祓式 （12月31日） == 文化財 == === 群馬県指定文化財 === * 重要文化財 ** 本殿（建造物） - 昭和38年9月4日指定。 ** 総社神社[[懸仏]] 2面（工芸品） - 昭和49年12月23日指定。 ** [[雲版]] 1面（工芸品） - 昭和51年5月7日指定。 ** 総社本上野国神名帳 1巻（書跡） - 昭和49年12月23日指定。 === 前橋市指定文化財 === * 重要文化財 ** 拝殿 - 平成5年4月16日指定。 * 重要無形民俗文化財 ** 総社神社の筒粥置炭式 - 平成5年4月16日指定。 ** 総社神社[[神楽|太々神楽]] - 昭和48年9月24日指定。 * 天然記念物 ** 総社神社の社叢けやき 6本 - 平成9年4月21日指定。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[群馬県]][[前橋市]]元総社町1丁目31番地45 '''交通アクセス''' * 鉄道：[[東日本旅客鉄道|JR東日本]][[上越線]]・[[両毛線]] [[新前橋駅]] （徒歩約20分） * バス：[[群馬中央バス]]　[[前橋駅]]～[[立川町 (前橋市)|立川町]]通り～[[新前橋駅]]西口線　総社神社南バス停または明神前バス停下車すぐ == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 神社由緒書 * 現地説明板 * {{Cite book|和書 |title=上野国神名帳の研究 |date=1974-12-10 |year=1974 |publisher=尾崎先生著書刊行会 |author=尾崎喜左雄 |last=尾崎 |first=喜左雄 |author-link=尾崎喜左雄}} * {{Cite book|和書 |title=群馬県史 |date=1993-5-27 |year=1993 |publisher=群馬県 |editor=群馬県史編さん委員会 |volume=通史編2 原始古代2}} * {{Cite book|和書 |title=前橋市史 |date=1971-2-1 |year=1971 |publisher=前橋市 |editor=前橋市史編さん委員会 |volume=第一巻}} * {{Cite book|和書 |title=前橋市史 |date=1984-2-1 |year=1984 |publisher=前橋市 |editor=前橋市史編さん委員会 |volume=第五巻}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=明治神社誌料編纂所|author=|year=1912|chapter=總社神社|title=[[府県郷社明治神社誌料]]|publisher=明治神社誌料編纂所|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|明治神社誌料|1912年}}}} * [{{NDLDC|1088244/504}} 『明治神社誌料 府県郷社 上』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）504-505コマ参照。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1987|chapter=総社神社|title=日本歴史地名体系 10 群馬県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582490107|ref={{Harvid|総社神社（平）|1987年}}}} == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Souja-jinja (Maebashi)}} * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ 上野国総社神社]（公式サイト） * [https://www.city.maebashi.gunma.jp/soshiki/kyoiku/bunkazaihogo/gyomu/3/2/1/5117.html 元総社・東の文化財を訪ねて／前橋市] {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:そうしやしんしや}} [[Category:前橋市の歴史]] [[Category:前橋市の建築物]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:群馬県の旧県社]] [[Category:群馬県の神社]] [[Category:上野国|社0]] [[Category:群馬県指定重要文化財]] [[Category:群馬県内の市町村指定有形文化財]]

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine Ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14th year }} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Shinto-stub}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Maebashi]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] }} [[sn:Sōja Shrine (Maebashi)]] [[sn:ōja Shrine (Maebashi)]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Pages without valid translation templates or en interwikis]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Sōja Shrine (Maebashi)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:Pages without valid translation templates or en interwikis or ja interwikis]] [[ja:総社神社 (前橋市)]] {{translated page|ja|総社神社 (前橋市)|version=102231104|comment=Imported full ja history}}

It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine Ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine Ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14th year }} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine Ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[:en:Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14th year }} and designated a Maebashi City [[sn:commons:Category:Souja-jinja (Maebashi)]][[ja:総社神社 (前橋市)]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q17220813]] Wikidata name: Sōja Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:39, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | location = 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}}
{{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}}
{{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}}
{{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}}
{{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[:en:Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine Ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[:en:Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14th year }} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from [[:en:Shin-Maebashi Station|Shin-Maebashi Station]] (JR [[:en:Jōetsu Line|Jōetsu Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[:en:Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine Ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[:en:Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14th year }} and designated a Maebashi City The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine Ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[:en:Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient [[:en:Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke Province]] (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine Ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the [[:en:Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke Province]]. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14th year }} and designated a Maebashi City {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|WD=Q1054838|lt=Kōzuke Province}} (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine Ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|WD=Q1054838|lt=Kōzuke Province}}. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14th year }} and designated a Maebashi City It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|WD=Q1054838|lt=Kōzuke Province|1=Kōzuke Province}} (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine Ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|WD=Q1054838|lt=Kōzuke Province|1=Kōzuke Province}}. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} | latitude = 36 | latm = 23 | lats = 16.80 | longitude = 139 | lonm = 2 | lons = 16.30 | type = Former Ken-sha (Prefectural Shrine) | style = {{nihongo|Nagare-zukuri|流造}} | alias = {{nihongo|Jōshū Sōja Shrine|上野国総社神社}} | map = Japan Gunma | established = {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}} period (traditional) | image = [[File:Souja-jinja (Maebashi) keidai.JPG|280px|Sōja Shrine precinct]] }} '''Sōja Shrine''' ({{nihongo|総社神社|そうじゃじんじゃ}}), formally known as '''Sōja Shrine of Jōshū''' (上野国総社神社), is a historic Shinto shrine located in Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture. It served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (central shrine) of the ancient {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|WD=Q1054838|lt=Kōzuke Province|1=Kōzuke Province}} (Jōshū). The shrine holds the status of a former {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}} under the modern Shinto shrine Ranking system. == Overview == In the {{nihongo|ancient period|古代}}, provincial governors ({{nihongo|Kokushi|国司}}) were required to visit and offer prayers at prominent shrines within their jurisdictions. As this practice evolved, {{nihongo|Sōja shrines|総社}} were established to consolidate the worship of these deities in a single location. Sōja Shrine became the central shrine for the {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|WD=Q1054838|lt=Kōzuke Province|1=Kōzuke Province}}. The shrine enshrines the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}} (Kōzuke Provincial deity Register), which lists the deities of the province. This register has been designated an Important Cultural Property by Gunma Prefecture. == Deities == === Main Deities === * {{nihongo|Iwatatsunoo no Mikoto|磐筒男命}} * {{nihongo|Iwatatsume no Mikoto|磐筒女命}} * {{nihongo|Ukanomitama no Mikoto|宇迦御魂命}} * {{nihongo|Futsunushi no Mikoto|経津主命}} * {{nihongo|Susanoo no Mikoto|須佐之男命}} === Subordinate Deities === The shrine also enshrines ten major deities mentioned in the {{nihongo|Jōshū Jinja Myōjin|上野国神名帳}}, including: * {{nihongo|Numakabo Daimyōjin|抜鉾大明神}} * {{nihongo|Akagi Daimyōjin|赤城大明神}} * {{nihongo|Ikaho Daimyōjin|伊香保大明神}} * {{nihongo|Haruna Daimyōjin|榛名大明神}} * {{nihongo|Asama Daimyōjin|浅間大明神}} == History == According to tradition, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{nihongo|Emperor Sujin|崇神天皇}}. Its current name, Sōja Shrine, reflects its role as the central shrine of Kōzuke Province. The shrine’s current location was established during the {{nihongo|Muromachi period|室町時代}}, following its relocation from an earlier site in Miyananabe (宮鍋). Historical records note its destruction during the wars of the {{nihongo|Sengoku period|戦国時代}} and its reconstruction during the {{nihongo|Momoyama period|桃山時代}}. In the {{nihongo|Meiji period|明治時代}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社}}. == Shrine Precincts == === Buildings === * '''main hall (Honden)''': A three-bay Nagare-zukuri structure, built in the {{nihongo|Keichō era|慶長年間}} and designated an Important Cultural Property. * '''Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Reconstructed in {{nihongo|1843|天保14th year }} and designated a Maebashi City Cultural Property. * '''Kaguraden''': A hall for sacred dances. === Cultural Properties === '''Gunma Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties''': * main hall (Honden) * {{nihongo|Kōzuke Provincial deity Register|上野国神名帳}} == festivals == * '''New Year’s Day festival''' (January 1) * '''Archery ceremony''' (January 6) * '''Otsutsu-gayu Fortune ceremony''' (January 15) * '''Spring festival''' (March 15) * '''Autumn festival''' (October 9) == Access == '''location''': 1-31-45 Moto Sōja-chō, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture '''Access''': * 20-minute walk from {{ill|Shin-Maebashi Station|en|Shin-Maebashi Station|WD=Q1652844|lt=Shin-Maebashi Station|1=Shin-Maebashi Station}} (JR {{ill|Jōetsu Line|en|Jōetsu Line|WD=Q1135061|lt=Jōetsu Line|1=Jōetsu Line}}). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.net-you.com/souja/ Official website of Sōja Shrine] {{Shinto-stub}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:総社神社 (前橋市)]] {{translated page|ja|総社神社 (前橋市)|version=102231104|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{wikidata link|Q17220813}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Buildings in Maebashi]] [[Category:Former_Prefectural_Shrines_in_Gunma_Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Maebashi, Gunma]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties Designated by Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Kōzuke Province]] [[Category:Maebashi]] [[Category:Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties in Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]]
